references.text: The same instruction regarding bringing an offering from the small livestock, including goats, as a thank offering to the Lord
The introduction to the chapter on thank offerings, establishing the principle of presenting the offering before the face of the Lord
Parallel text concerning bringing lambs as a thank offering before the face of the Lord, with the same structure as the goat offering
A male goat used as a sin offering, illustrating the role of goats in the sacrificial system
Supplementary regulations regarding thank offerings that include goats among the permitted sacrificial animals
Requirements for sacrificial animals from cattle, sheep, or goats to be without defect
A goat used as a sin offering, confirming the place of goats within the sacrificial system
Parallel liturgical structure: Both show presentation and slaughter before the face of the Lord for the sin offering and peace offering respectively.
Direct complementary text: 3:6 covers lambs/sheep and 3:12 covers goats within the same peace offering legislation.
Theological contrast: 3:12 defines the requirement for a clean sacrificial animal, while 27:11 defines the consequence for an unclean one.
